arcs.title: The Duck Bandit
arcs.summary: Day 4: The fifth duck has arrived — teal, with a hand-stitched copper-green flat cap containing a white-thread monogram, 'E.H.,' on the inner band. Lucy found the monogram within forty seconds. Steve has confirmed the first initial on the conditioner tin base is E; the second is partially legible under improved lighting. The Bandit's shape is very nearly in focus: the initials E.H., pre-1980 charm-work, old-growth eastern ridge, a practitioner who learned before Ministry licensing, and a talent for millinery. Day 5 should be the reveal — Steve resolves the second initial on the tin (H), the name E.H. clicks into place, the Bandit is identified (a figure connected to the eastern ridge, older, known to at least one of them or to the family, who has been leaving ducks as a form of wordless affection or trail-marking). The reveal should be warm and satisfying, not dramatic. Lucy should be acknowledged as having known substantially longer than anyone else.
